item.content:encoded:
I gotta say, I thought the premise as I thought it was was interesting. That being, the Foundation attempting to affect their own narrative. I liked that they picked up on the author pages not being subject to the usual deletion rules; that they probed their own narrative structure. Grabbing other fictional characters is also something of a cool idea. Very meta.

Trouble is, I think it started the descent into over-the-top cringey places at about the character list. It felt like a big let-down when I realised it was turning into an over-the-top jab at meta with an apparent total lack of subtletly.

It's really the sort of thing I just cannot like, so I've downvoted it.

item.title: I want Gordon to enter my author page with violent intent, killing its pacing instantly.
item.content:encoded:
And here… we… go!

This page, when everything is out, will in fact function as my author page as well as a tale. Those sections will be released over the next week or so, as indicated. This is primarily a way to break up the reading experience, prevent reader fatigue. I fully admit to Kalinin's 001 inspiring this structure - I think it's a great way to do things! Three of the four parts coming are written fully already, so barring some crazy unexpected thing happening, there shouldn't be any delays. Be advised I'm at GMT, so adjust for your timezone accordingly before giving out to me for being late.

Anyway, yeah, this is also the intro for what will hopefully be a full tale series about the Pataphysics Department1. Penelope will definitely be a continuing presence, and the MTF members will probably end up popping up now and then. I look forward to seeing you there.

Thanks to swn-001-1-ADLDR, swn001-1-ABSNL and swn001-1-SHDRL for looking at various drafts of this throughout its early stages, especially bae for putting up with endless PMs where spouted pretentious ideas for subsequent tales and the overall structure of this thing. They're the best. Thanks to swn001-1-ASWN and swn-001-1-MCLN for being the primary inspirations for what I'm doing here, in very different ways.

Since this is my author page, I'd also like to thank some people who have been big influences for me in a more general sense, particularly when it comes to writing. Nicknames used when referring to real people in my life.

This is a little long
– hide block
  • JK Rowling, Eoin Colfer, RL Stein and Dav Pilkey for helping to foster a love of reading in me as a kid, and for giving me a taste of all the things you can do with writing.
  • My Dad, for bringing me to the library so many damn times, for encouraging me to push my comfort zone in the fiction I read, for a surname nobody can pronounce, for giving a damn when I got back into writing this year, for being someone I can always talk to, for giving me a model to aspire towards in warmth, humour, empathy and honesty, for passing on the gene that makes us take way too long to tell a story.
  • CTYI, for providing me almost all of my dearest friends, for teaching me I could make friends without having to hide my rough edges, for fifteen weeks of my life that have helped me understand who I am.
  • Omino, for putting up with me talking for actual hours about my skip ideas, for being the best friend to a kid who needed one more than you knew, for what probably amounts to months of my life hanging out with you, staying up too late and watching crappy action movies.
  • Entropy, for punching me in the face that one time, for helping me give less of a shit, for reintroducing me to the SCP wiki a long time back.
  • Casablanca, for being a wonderfully terrible English teacher, for blatantly judging me more harshly than other students in your class because you knew I wasn't pushing myself, for two years of weirdness.
  • Sunflower, most important of all, for being an editor and a friend, for showing me how integral research is to good writing, for teaching me a million tiny tricks I use in everything I write, for being funny and genuine and uncompromising, for providing an escape and distraction from the unbearable pressure of the Leaving Cert, for doing a phenomenal amount of work to get some stupid kids freaking published. Your legacy lives on in the thousands of lives you touched and the communities you established. I probably haven't the slightest understanding of the scope of your work in the Irish writing community, and it kills me that I'll never be able to talk to you about that, I'll never be able to show you my work here, never get to tell you how much you meant to me.

That's it for now. Catch y'all in the next author note.

Footnotes
1. Apologies to Alfred Jarry for butchering that term somewhat - in-universe, Penelope Panagiotopolous named it that because it was a catchy pseudoscience buzzword that most readers wouldn't question.
